packet_dag.terminal_condition: The Rabbi / One Time Operations shell shows Rabbi-facing primary modules, demotes raw platform support modules, keeps support routes deep-linkable, and preserves workspace access boundaries.

title: Operations IA Nav And Filter Alignment

reasons: Latest Operations screenshots show the One Time sidebar still exposing generic platform modules such as Dashboard, Watchdog, Agents, Studio, Integrations, and Reporting as first-class Rabbi navigation.

The repo already contains a Rabbi-facing IA model that demotes raw support modules behind Platform Support and groups the work around Overview, Members, Classes, Communications, Automations, Payments, Tasks, and Setup.
The fix can be scoped to the live Operations shell navigation presentation while leaving backend allowed views, data scopes, route access, and external provider behavior unchanged.
ramble_router.next_exact_packet: After this IA/nav/filter alignment, continue CRM contact-detail polish or any manual visual defects found by the latest audit.

operator_intent_summary: Make the Rabbi / One Time Operations app feel clean and self-explanatory by replacing the raw platform sidebar with Rabbi-facing module labels and section-aware navigation while preserving diagnostic support access.

decisions_captured.decision: Production deploy/live-smoke target is still required before terminal app-visible Done.

out_of_scope: No backend authorization, allowed-view policy, database query, route registry, action registry, payment, email, access grant, account, DNS, send, publish, upload, or external-provider mutation.
No GHL runtime, LeadConnector runtime, external CRM client, or external CRM write.
No removal of diagnostic support routes used by Shloimie/Codex; this packet only demotes them from the primary Rabbi sidebar.
affected_surfaces: One Time Operations top context strip
One Time module filter rail labels

inspection_targets: public/operations.html workspaceNavViewIds, workspaceNavItems, renderSidebar, renderSidebarModuleList, currentNavItem, switchView, setCurrentSection
known_blockers: Production deploy/live-smoke remains blocked until a target is explicit.
observed_visual_defects: One Time sidebar shows raw platform-first items such as Dashboard, Watchdog, Agents, Integrations, and Reporting.

The first-level IA splits related Rabbi work into too many visible modules: Program, Members, Community, Studio, Content, Live, Schedule, Communications, Tasks, Automations, Integrations, and Reporting.
Payment / Access exists only as a crowded top tab under Program rather than a first-class Rabbi work module.
Support diagnostics are not visually demoted behind a Platform Support affordance.

expanded_phrases.clean: The sidebar should read as a Rabbi-facing work console, not a raw internal platform index.
expanded_phrases.even: Primary modules should use consistent short labels, markers, section targets, and active states across desktop and mobile.
expanded_phrases.loads nicely: The first rendered Operations viewport should expose the relevant One Time modules without a long platform-module wall or layout jump.
expanded_phrases.CRM: Interpret CRM as first-party BNA member/contact workflow UX only; do not add GHL, LeadConnector, external CRM APIs, or external CRM writes.
expanded_phrases.community section: Community/class work remains first-party One Time classroom/community data and may be grouped under Rabbi modules without cross-workspace record bleed.

product_quality_expansion.first_party_pattern_interpretation: Use the existing Rabbi IA and first-party BNA Operations routes. Support modules remain routable for diagnostics but are demoted from the Rabbi-facing primary sidebar.

requirements.statement: Align the live One Time Operations sidebar and module labels to the Rabbi-facing IA, demoting raw support/platform modules while preserving direct diagnostic access.
requirements.expected_result: Desktop and mobile Operations screenshots show primary Rabbi modules for Overview, Members, Classes, Comms, Automations, Payments, Tasks, and Setup, plus a Platform Support footer affordance; Agents/Integrations/Reporting/Watchdog remain deep-linkable but are not first-class Rabbi sidebar buttons.
acceptance_criteria: The service-provider sidebar no longer renders Dashboard, Watchdog, Agents, Integrations, Reporting, Studio, Live, or Schedule as primary One Time sidebar buttons.
The primary One Time sidebar renders Rabbi-facing module labels and markers with section-aware active states, including a Payments item that opens the Program Payment / Access section.
A demoted Platform Support control remains available for support diagnostics without changing backend allowed views or route access.
Direct support route switches such as agents and integrations continue to render when explicitly opened.
Desktop and mobile screenshots have no horizontal overflow, clipped sidebar labels, console errors, or top context mismatches for the affected routes.

criteria: Raw source and broad UI cleanup register exist for RAW-20260702-008.
The latest visual audit and manual screenshot review identify raw platform navigation as a remaining One Time Operations cleanup defect.
The existing Rabbi IA model names the desired primary groups and support demotion behavior.
The code path separating allowed routes from visible sidebar presentation is identifiable in public/operations.html.
The implementation is scoped to navigation presentation and tests, with no data, auth, registry, or external-provider mutation.
